metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:embedding_collapse_score: Sample up to 2048 real-item embeddings, seed 42, excluding padding/reserved tokens. Map mean off-diagonal pairwise cosine to [0,1]; denominator k*(k-1). Higher indicates directional alignment, not measured recommendation diversity. Existing convention returns zero for at most two items.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:embedding_sample_count: Number of real-item embeddings sampled for the collapse probe; pairwise denominator is k*(k-1).
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_mean: Mean positive-minus-negative model score across valid training-loader positions in at most ten batches; positive, negative and sequence IDs must be nonzero. Larger means stronger sampled separation; denominator is valid_positions in the breakdown.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_p10: Nearest-rank lower tenth percentile of the same valid training-position margins, index ceil(0.1*N); lower indicates weaker sampled separation. Null if N=0.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate: Fraction of the same N valid training positions whose sampled negative score exceeds positive score; lower is better. Null if N=0.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_small_margin_rate: Fraction of the same N valid training positions with positive-minus-negative score below eps=0.5; lower indicates fewer small margins. Null if N=0.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_category_br: Counts low-margin and wrong-rank valid training positions and their denominator. Item-category metadata is unavailable, so category lists remain empty; these lists are unrelated to dataset routing.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:pos_neg_margin_frequency_b: Stratify the same sampled training positions by positive-item training-interaction frequency: 1-4, 5-19, 20+. Each stratum reports its position denominator, mean margin and negative-beats-positive fraction. Frequency is not exposure.
metric_definitions.Movies_and_TV:execution_checks: At atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4, compare individual unpadded and batched left-padded aligned valid features, maximum-nonzero-position readouts and fixed candidate scores, including singleton/empty rows, a standalone all-padding batch and added leading zeros within the existing window. Compare ModelView scores with the actual trained module's score_candidates prediction entry point for every checked row. Empty sequence features must be zero; trained score biases remain included. Check BxLxK scoring against loop references. Report dtype, maximum discrepancies and failures; no checkpoint repair occurs here.

Movies_and_TV:temporal_sensitivity.population: At most 200 uniformly sampled eligible training users without replacement in sorted ID order, RNG 42, per actual dataset ModelView. One uniformly selected training target index with at least five preceding interactions; truncate its prefix once to the existing model window. Require five retained items. Report eligible, sampled, retained, exclusion and unique-key counts. These targets may have been used in training.
Movies_and_TV:temporal_sensitivity.candidates: Target plus 99 unique negatives drawn independently of official evaluation. Exclude the original full training history and target before perturbation, as in the supplied validation sampler; preserve prior target occurrences in inputs. Freeze candidate IDs for all conditions. Exclude insufficient-candidate users. Target rank is one-based, sorting by descending model score then ascending item ID.
Movies_and_TV:temporal_sensitivity.interventions: For retained length n, k=max(1,floor((n-1)/4)). Unchanged, oldest-k deletion, most-recent-k deletion among the first n-1 positions, five uniform random-k deletions among those positions, five independent within-block permutations of the first n-1 positions with block size three, final-item removal, and last-item-only. Preserve survivor chronology and the final item except in explicit removal. Never refill; left-pad every variant to the same width. Average repeated scalar effects within each user before aggregation. Local shuffling can create implausible chronology.
Movies_and_TV:temporal_sensitivity.rank_change: Perturbed rank minus intact rank per retained user; positive means ranking damage. Means divide by reported contributing user counts.
Movies_and_TV:temporal_sensitivity.hr10_change: Perturbed indicator(rank<=10) minus intact indicator(rank<=10) per retained user; negative means ranking damage. Means divide by reported contributing user counts.
Movies_and_TV:temporal_sensitivity.cosine_distance: One minus cosine of perturbed and intact final states; larger means state movement. Null when either norm is below 1e-8. Report valid-repeat and user denominators. Representation movement alone does not establish utility damage.
Movies_and_TV:temporal_sensitivity.normalized_displacement: L2 state difference divided by max(intact-state L2 norm,1e-8), averaged over repeats then users; larger means relative state movement.
Movies_and_TV:temporal_sensitivity.summaries: Descriptive category means, intact diagnostic HR@10 and history-length 5-9/10-19/20+ and repeat/novel slices. Repeat means target occurred before its training index, even outside the retained window. Denominators and sparse/constant flags accompany each result. user_outcomes caches paired scalar outcomes for host aggregation; it contains no validation or test labels.
Movies_and_TV:temporal_sensitivity.uncertainty: 2000 CPU bootstrap replicates, separate RNG 42, resampling users with replacement within this category and preserving paired conditions. Percentile 2.5th-97.5th intervals require at least 30 unique users with complete outcomes. Four-category point estimates require all four category records and equal category weights; four-category intervals additionally require at least 30 contributing users in every category, including within each slice. This single-view API cannot manufacture missing categories, so macro fields are null with reasons. An available-category summary is explicitly descriptive and separate.
Movies_and_TV:temporal_sensitivity.limits: Conditional in-sample sensitivity given fitted checkpoints, selected prefixes and candidates; intervals omit seed variability, new-category generalization and validation-search selection optimism. Simulator users and their required full-catalog recommendations remain separate. No inference about intent, exposure, ratings, reviews or simulator traits is supported. Official macro validation HR@10 alone selects models.
